src/components/viewport/UnitObject.tsx.label: host-math
src/components/viewport/UnitObject.tsx.why: the dental viewport object: puts a world-space pick into unit-local coordinates and normalises a face normal, for painting, zones, tips and the rim. Grew from 5 to 6 when a rim press stopped asking an armed tool what it meant and started asking where it landed (rim/rimTarget.ts), which needs the surface normal at the press to seat an inserted handle

src/components/viewport/viewportPort.ts.label: host-math
src/components/viewport/viewportPort.ts.why: three.js camera projection for the ViewportPort seam, and the unit normal of one picked triangle (render-side picking answer)

src/core/surfacePath/frame.ts.label: host-math
src/core/surfacePath/frame.ts.why: the fitted plane and 2D frame of a loop drawn on a surface (centroid, normal, basis, planar area): portable core geometry by design, no engine call and no renderer

src/core/surfacePath/resample.ts.label: host-math
src/core/surfacePath/resample.ts.why: walks a drawn path at a spacing and interpolates each sample and its normal; putting the sample back on the surface is the callers injected pick, not done here

src/core/surfacePath/spline.ts.label: host-math
src/core/surfacePath/spline.ts.why: the centripetal Catmull-Rom span between two drawn anchors: knot spacing (one pow, one hypot through vec3) and the Barry-Goldman pyramid, all of it plain interpolation between points the operator placed. It decides nothing about the model - the samples are projected onto the surface by the callers injected pick, and the rim plane, side and mask stay the engine s

src/dental/rim/drawnRim.ts.label: host-math
src/dental/rim/drawnRim.ts.why: normalises the anchor normal to aim one projection ray; the geometry that matters - the plane, the side and the visibility mask - is all the engine's, which is the entire reason this call exists

src/dental/rim/rimDraftGeometry.ts.label: host-math
src/dental/rim/rimDraftGeometry.ts.why: where the drawn rim sits for the viewport: the lift off the surface along an anchor normal, and the two reach tests (nearest anchor, close-the-loop). Render and hit-testing only - the rim the ENGINE is given is resampled by core/surfacePath, not here

src/dental/rim/rimTarget.ts.label: host-math
src/dental/rim/rimTarget.ts.why: what a press on the rim means: whether it landed on a handle, on the drawn line, or on bare model. It compares distances through vec3 and samples the span curve through core/surfacePath/spline; it decides an INTERACTION, never geometry - the point it hands back is one the curve already passes through, and the rim the engine is given is resampled and rebuilt as before

src/dental/rim/seedFromDetected.ts.label: host-math
src/dental/rim/seedFromDetected.ts.why: picks the handles the operator will drag off a DETECTED rim: arc length between its own points, and the heading either side of one measured over a millimetre so scanner jitter does not sprinkle handles along a straight run. Grew from 1 to 3 hits when spacing alone proved to miss corners. It decides nothing geometric - the points are detections, kept exactly, and the plane, the side and the mask are rebuilt by the engine when the drawing is done

src/dental/rim/useRimDrawing.ts.label: host-adapter
src/dental/rim/useRimDrawing.ts.why: imports inverseTransformPoint/Direction to put a world-space pick into unit-local coordinates before storing it; no geometry of its own

src/items/thumbnail.ts.label: host-math
src/items/thumbnail.ts.why: the thumbnail camera: the distance at which a bounding sphere fills a square frame. Render framing only - no print decision rests on it

src/supports/useSupportEdits.ts.label: host-adapter
src/supports/useSupportEdits.ts.why: what a pointer does to supports: converts a world-space hit to unit-local and hands off to the shared planAddTip / contactToRemove. No geometry of its own; the snapping and the reach test are the engine host package
